GHG emissions reductions are achieved through reduction in electricity including aeration energy for degradation of organics and BNR (scope 2), reduction in chemicals including methanol for BNR, PAA for disinfection, magnesium chloride for phosphorus (P) recovery, and polymer for dewatering (scope 3), and reductions in direct emissions of CO , N O, and CH from the 2 2 4 wastewater treatment process (scope 1). There are no plans for commercialization of the products from this project. The ML Toolkit is a publicly accessible website. While it targets users in the water industry, it is available to anyone who accesses the site. Providing open access via the ML Toolkit allows utilities to design methods that will work for them. Also, being open access provides opportunities for broader involvement toward innovative solutions since the protocols are not locked down and owned by a few. xviii The Water Research Foundation The plant process flow diagram shows the locations of the 5 Applications which demonstrate a whole plant approach for data-driven process controls. The ML Toolkit framework and key disciplines needed for each step are shown in Figure ES-2. Figure ES-2. ML Toolkit Framework including the Steps in ML Implementation and Key Disciplines Needed. Five case studies of data-driven process controls in real full-scale facilities at DC Water, HRSD, and Metro Water Recovery were developed and demonstrated for five promising Applications. Each case study followed the steps used in the ML Toolkit framework approach outlined in Figure ES-2.
